title: Transport for NSW launches the PAWS AI animal-detection and smart-signage trial on the Monaro Highway between Bredbo and Williamsdale; no outcome yet
summary: Transport for NSW's Protective Animal Warning System: two AI-enabled roadside cameras on a 13 km Monaro Highway stretch trigger driver warnings; trial announced 18 Jul 2026, no results yet.
account: About Regional reported on 18 July 2026 that Transport for NSW developed the Protective Animal Warning System (PAWS), with two AI-enabled cameras being placed along the Monaro Highway between Bredbo and Williamsdale on a 13 km stretch. Heat-sensing and optical roadside cameras detect animals on or near the road and use an AI model trained to identify common species such as kangaroos, koalas, deer and wombats; the solar-powered cameras trigger signs telling drivers to slow down. The trial was expected to start in August 2026 and, per the report, to run until 2027/2028; Member for Monaro Steve Whan welcomed it. The NSW Government media release of 18 July 2026 named in Google News could not be fetched. No detection, driver response or collision outcome has been reported; the date used is the news report's publication date.
purpose: Detect wildlife near the road and warn drivers dynamically to limit wildlife-vehicle strikes; no benefit has yet been observed.
